description:
In February 2002, Immersion Corporation sued Sony, and Microsoft, for patent infringement over the vibration technology in the DualShock controller. Nintendo wasn't named: its Rumble Pak used a separately patented design.

Microsoft settled straight away, buying a 10% stake in Immersion. Sony fought the case instead. That decision cost it years in court and tens of millions more than Microsoft ever paid.

A jury awarded Immersion $82 million on 21 September 2004; with interest, the total reached $90.7 million. A federal court upheld the verdict in March 2006 and ordered Sony to stop selling the infringing controllers, though the order was stayed during appeal.

At E3 2006, Sony announced the new PlayStation 3 controller would ship with no vibration at all. Sony said this avoided interference with the controller's new motion sensor; Immersion's own president was publicly sceptical of that explanation.
